one-check-per-line.why: all 2 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 2

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 2 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I checked both verifier checks against their expect lines. Check 1 passes when "the --tsv command prints a JSON array equal to the array the plain command prints for the CSV form of the same table." It fails on an error, on output that is not an array, or on a mismatch. That is what "the same JSON array" requires. Comparing the outputs as parsed JSON keeps it lenient. The phrase "rows keyed by the header row" adds nothing in practice: the plain command already keys rows by the header ('[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]'), so equal arrays are keyed too. Check 2 passes when README mentions `--tsv` and either says it is for tab-separated input or shows it in a usage example. That is a fair reading of "documents." The stricter tests are all under "Advisory (not pass/fail)": `npm test` passing, a new test being added, and byte-for-byte output with the trailing newline. No PASS or FAIL condition demands a mutation test, a branch rule or exact wording.

runs-as-written.why: The criterion holds for every command in both briefs. Each one names files or scripts that exist: bin/csv2json.js and test/csv.test.js are tracked, and `npm test` maps to the "node --test" script. The `--tsv` flag is added by builder step 1 before any command uses it. The verifier's `printf '...\t...' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv > /tmp/tsv.out` lines are valid shell, since printf turns \t into tabs. The `node -e "..."` snippet is valid shell: inside double quotes it contains no `$`, backticks or `!`. It is also valid JavaScript (JSON.parse, readFileSync, a ternary). `npm install` only runs if package.json lists dependencies, which is fine. `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` is a usage example to put in the README, not a command anyone is told to run. No command breaks.

catches-traps.why: Item 1 is met. The builder brief says to keep the output format "so CSV output does not change", to "Keep the existing tests passing" and to "Run `npm test` and confirm every test passes". Item 3 is met. Check 1 pipes the same tables through as TSV and as CSV and compares the parsed JSON ("SAME"/"DIFF"). Item 2 is only partly met. The Advisory section, marked "not pass/fail", does suggest "Run `npm test` and note whether it passes" and asks the verifier to note the plain CSV output. But it never says that no expect line covers CSV behaviour or npm test. The item requires that statement, and the brief only implies it by putting these points under Advisory. So the briefs do not handle every must_catch item.

avoids-must-not.why: The verifier brief has exactly two checks, one for each expect line in order: "Check 1" covers the --tsv/CSV JSON equivalence and "Check 2" covers the README. npm test and exact CSV output appear only under "Advisory (not pass/fail)". They are labelled as notes and have no PASS or FAIL condition, so I don't count them as a third check. Check 1's PASS and FAIL conditions only compare the --tsv and CSV outputs as parsed JSON. Check 2's conditions only look at whether README.md mentions --tsv. Neither one requires npm test or the CSV tests to pass. The builder brief does say to run `npm test`, but both must_not items are about the verifier's checks and PASS/FAIL conditions, so that isn't a violation. Neither must_not item applies.

methods-private.why:
I compared the builder brief's steps with the verifier brief's checks, and the builder brief contains a probe that the verifier also uses. In step 2 the builder is told to test `--tsv` with input 'a	b
1	2
' against CSV 'a,b
1,2
', with the expected output '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
'. Check 1 in the verifier brief runs the same comparison: "Repeat the comparison with a two-column table: TSV 'a	b
1	2
' against CSV 'a,b
1,2
'". Its advisory also uses the same exact output, '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
'. The builder may write its own tests, but this one copies the verifier's inputs and expected output, which tells the builder exactly what will be checked. The rest of the builder brief is fine: running `npm test`, the implementation steps and the README step contain no PASS/FAIL conditions.
